task.title: Close the CLI exit-code denylists so a strict mode accepts only a pass
task.description: An independent recheck found that the security command's exit-code folds are denylists rather than exhaustive mappings, so a continuous-integration run exits zero on a needs-approval gate and is therefore more permissive than the enforced mode, which contradicts the governing policy that strict continuous integration accepts only a pass. Two fold sites were identified in src/commands/security.ts. Replace both with exhaustive mappings over the recognized gate values, so pass exits zero and fail, needs-approval, incomplete and any unrecognized value exit non-zero in a strict mode, with the message naming which of the three non-pass outcomes occurred without echoing raw error text, a path or source bytes. Keep the advisory mode's existing permissiveness, and keep the distinction between a violation, an approval requirement and unavailable evidence visible in the output. The service-level folds were already made exhaustive by an earlier task; align the command layer with them rather than inventing a second vocabulary, and check whether any other command surface reads a gate value the same way. Regression first: add tests that fail before and pass after for a needs-approval gate in continuous-integration mode, an incomplete gate, an unrecognized gate value, and the pass control, and confirm the advisory behavior is unchanged. Write T38-spec.md before coding, then T38-implementation.md and T38-result.json. Do not review your own fix.

acceptance_criteria: AC8: no required failed or incomplete check is relabeled PASS at any surface, including the process exit code; strict modes accept only a pass.

Policy fold (policies.md): FAIL on an established threshold violation; INCOMPLETE when a required check is missing, skipped, unparsed or unfinished; strict CI accepts only PASS; an optional skip warns and is never signed as passed; messages are constant and leak-safe.
The command layer and the service layer agree: a gate value that blocks in the service does not exit zero at the command, and an unrecognized value is treated as non-pass rather than falling through.
